name: p-shed
description: Scheduler/launcher for Claude Code headless runs. Cron-scheduled jobs launch `claude -p` in a folder, with per-job model, reasoning effort, timeout, duplicate guard, missed-tick catch-up, log rotation, a process-level circuit breaker that treats a Claude usage-limit / transient API overload as a skip (not a failure) so a quota window never trips it, and a task-level self-pause marker. Optional per-job guard command gates each launch (exit 0 = launch, 75 = quiet skip, else breaker-counted error) — guard-only jobs give free scheduled commands under full supervision; a guard's last stdout line is kept as `lastGuard.reason` and shown in `status`, so a quiet slot (which writes no history row) still explains itself. Reversible global pause, a status snapshot, and honest teardown that reports whether it actually removed the cron entry (and can kill in-flight jobs). Pure scheduler — no task storage. A maintenance window is a first-class command: `deploy` waits for the loop to go idle, pauses it, runs a command with its output passed through, and always releases — reclaiming its own pause via the next tick if the deploying process is killed. Speed profiles make pace one word: an optional `profiles:` table in jobs.yml maps a name to per-job schedule/model/effort/timeoutSec/enabled overrides, applied in memory (jobs.yml is never rewritten) by tick, status and run alike, and the ACTIVE name is resolved from PSHED_PROFILE, then a file outside the scheduled repository, then defaults.profile — so the one control that belongs to the operator is not stored where the loop can turn it. A profile problem never halts the tick. Commands (tool `pshed`): tick, run, install-cron, remove-cron, set-job, rm-job, reset-breaker, pause, resume, profile show/set/list, status, stop, wait-idle, deploy. Skills: init, start, stop, job, reset-breaker.
